title.zh: Maxwellian 等离子体色散函数

summary: Evaluate dimensionless Maxwellian w and Z with an explicit existing numerical path, preserving the direct SciPy default.

capability: Evaluate dimensionless Maxwellian w and Z with an explicit existing numerical path, preserving the direct SciPy default.
operation: evaluate Maxwellian dispersion with a selected numerical approximation
discovery.model: One Maxwellian relation with direct SciPy, tunable rational, distinct fixed64 and tabulated J-pole numerical paths.
discovery.geometry: No spatial geometry; pointwise complex function evaluation.
discovery.boundary: Both complex128 outputs must be finite. Each approximation retains its own sampled evidence and continuation limits.

identity.relation: Dimensionless complex phase argument to Maxwellian w and Z values or the selected approximation
identity.definition: w(z)=exp(-z^2) erfc(-i z), Z(z)=i sqrt(pi) w(z). SciPy uses scipy.special.wofz; rational and fixed64 retain distinct existing evaluations. J-pole returns the tabulated Z_J and w_J=Z_J/(i sqrt(pi)), both at the selected finite order.
identity.model: One Maxwellian relation with direct SciPy, tunable rational, distinct fixed64 and tabulated J-pole numerical paths.
identity.geometry: No spatial geometry; pointwise complex function evaluation
identity.coordinates: Complex argument plane, with the imaginary sign preserved
identity.boundary: Both complex128 outputs must be finite. Each approximation retains its own sampled evidence and continuation limits.
assumptions: The caller has already mapped frequency, wave number, drift and thermal speed to a dimensionless z using one explicit convention.
No dispersion root or physical mode is inferred from the function value.

inputs.name: z
inputs.description: Already normalized complex phase argument, evaluated elementwise.
inputs.shape: scalar or any nonempty array shape
inputs.constraints: All elements finite after complex128 conversion; masked, boolean, string, nonnumeric and empty inputs are rejected.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: Existing numerical path; scipy preserves the direct calculation.
inputs.constraints: Exactly scipy, rational, weideman or jpole.

inputs.name: order
inputs.description: Numerical truncation or pole count; None means omitted control.
inputs.constraints: Rational: None selects 32, any positive integer allowed. J-pole: None selects 8, or 8/12/16/24. Scipy and weideman: None only. Boolean rejected.

outputs.name: w
outputs.description: Faddeeva value or selected approximation. J-pole returns Z_J/(i sqrt(pi)), not exact w.
outputs.shape: same as z; scalar input yields a zero-dimensional array
outputs.constraints: Finite and representable; same finite-order approximation as Z.

outputs.name: Z
outputs.description: Maxwellian plasma dispersion value or selected approximation, normalized as i sqrt(pi) w.
outputs.shape: same as z; scalar input yields a zero-dimensional array
outputs.constraints: Both w and Z must be finite and representable for the entire call.

preconditions: The caller supplies a finite dimensionless argument using one explicit normalization convention.
Both w and final Z must fit finite complex128.
supported: Pointwise real or complex arguments, including representable upper and lower half-plane values.
Scalar or nonempty array input with shape and input values preserved.
excluded: Thermal-speed, drift and wave-number convention conversion; dispersion matrix assembly and root finding.
A global approximation error guarantee or experimental validation.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: TypeError for masked, boolean, string or nonnumeric z, unsupported method or unusable order; ValueError for empty, ragged or nonfinite z after complex128 conversion.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: FloatingPointError if either w or final Z is nonfinite; unexpected backend execution errors propagate. No clamp or fallback is applied.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; no iterative solve is exposed.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial result; one unrepresentable element fails the entire call.

example.description: Evaluate all four existing numerical paths and their common scientific outputs.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.kinetic import evaluate_plasma_dispersion
result = evaluate_plasma_dispersion(0j, method='scipy')
assert result['w'] == 1
assert np.isclose(result['Z'], 1j * np.sqrt(np.pi))
rational = evaluate_plasma_dispersion(0.2+0.7j, method='rational', order=16)
fixed64 = evaluate_plasma_dispersion(0.2+0.7j, method='weideman')
jpole = evaluate_plasma_dispersion(0.2+0.7j, method='jpole', order=12)
assert all(set(r) == {'w', 'Z'} for r in (rational, fixed64, jpole))
assert all(np.isfinite(r['Z']) for r in (rational, fixed64, jpole))
example.expected: The SciPy origin has w=1 and Z=i sqrt(pi); every method returns exactly finite w and Z at the bounded sample.

scope: All original scientific references remain on their corresponding numerical paths; detailed scope is method-specific.
Common Result(w,Z), explicit control/default/rejection behavior, whole-array failures and lazy imports are exercised separately from numerical accuracy.

Independent 40-digit Faddeeva reference w(z)=exp(-z^2)erfc(-iz) from mpmath at mp.dps=40 over twelve upper-half-plane points, with the per-method budgets fixed before measurement: scipy and rational order 32 at 1e-11 relative, the fixed-order Weideman kernel at 1e-4, and the tabulated jpole family at 5e-5.
Z=i*sqrt(pi)*w asserted as algebra for all four methods, the exact reflection w(-conj z)=conj(w(z)) with Z(-conj z)=-conj(Z(z)), and the large-|z| asymptotic Z=-1/z+O(z**-3) probed at |z|=1e3.
verification.evidence_ceiling: test_plasma_dispersion_evidence.py compares every method with the closed-form Faddeeva definition at 40 digits and reports the observed maximum relative deviation per method inside the declared budget. The scaling identity, the reflection identity and the leading asymptotic are exact statements about the returned pair. These are observations on a twelve-point grid; no continuous-domain error bound, no lower-half-plane accuracy claim and no accuracy statement near the real axis where |w| varies fastest are established. The weideman and jpole entries remain truncation- and model-limited.
known_limitations: Caller thermal-speed, drift and wave-number normalization is not inferred or converted.
Approximation precision and continuation limits remain method-specific.
One unrepresentable output element rejects the whole array; independent mathematical w may still succeed.

The per-method accuracy statements are observed maxima on a twelve-point grid, not a proved continuous-domain bound; the fixed-order Weideman kernel and the tabulated jpole family remain truncation- and model-limited.
The reflection and asymptotic identities constrain symmetry and the leading large-|z| term; neither establishes accuracy inside the lower half plane or near the real axis.
